docs.purpose: The list of every scheduled offer: its placement, advertiser, targeting, flight days, whether it is on, whether its placement is oversubscribed and whether its target resolves to a report scenario. Each row opens the offer in the form or turns it on or off.
docs.data_story: It reads offers joined to advertisers and placements through the placements read; over_cap and resolvable are computed on the server.
docs.under_126: **GENERATED.** Rendered by the web LIST binding (mantine-datatable) from render.list on the shared binding standard: rows from the read's offers array, an edit action that opens the offer FORM in the Modal and a toggle_active action (a 50 px button, trim 4).

inputs.why: One QUERY contract returns the offers with server-computed flags; the page reads it on the server first and passes plain data.

outputs.why: The writes are the edit (the offer FORM) and the toggle (PATCH on the offer contract); the list refreshes from the server after each.
evidence: contract_admin_offer_upsert
outputs.rollback: None is applied locally, so none is undone: the list re-reads after the server answers.

state.why: An RSC page: the rows arrive from the server per request and refresh after a mutation; sort state is a local view choice.

staleness.why: Read per request (no-store); a stale toggle is refused with 409 by the updated_at check.
evidence: src/app/api/admin/placements/route.ts — Cache-Control private, no-store

session.why: An /admin/** page: classifyRoute returns "admin" for any pathname starting with /admin/, and "admin" is the profiles.is_admin flag checked in-predicate, not a Postgres role.
evidence: src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:162 — pathname === "/admin" || pathname.startsWith("/admin/") returns "admin"
src/lib/auth/route-guard.ts:159 — /api/admin/ returns "admin" for the contract half
migrations/226_profiles_admin_bootstrap.sql:27 — is_admin BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false
docs/specs/00-architecture/114_rls_policy_catalog.md §2 — there is no admin Postgres role; admin is a column flag checked inside the policy predicate

rls_class.why: The page writes offers and advertisers, Class B by Spec 114 §2 with the ONE ruled admin-read pattern (RLS on, one <table>_select_admin policy, no write policy); MF-40 D-1 (operator 2026-11-10) drops the move to an advertiser class (admin input only). placements, which it reads, is Class E (one public select policy, seed-only). The routes read and write through the owner connection, so the policies are defence in depth.
evidence: docs/specs/00-architecture/114_rls_policy_catalog.md §2 dated notes 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-10 — the admin-read pattern (offers, advertisers); placements Class E

checks.why: R-12: each toggle writes exactly one admin_audit_log row (offer_activate or offer_deactivate) in the same transaction (src/tests/admin-placements.infra.test.ts).

errors.why: Every admin route handler is wrapped by withApiEnvelope, which returns { data, error, meta } with a sanitised code on any throw; the surface renders from that envelope rather than from a raw exception.
evidence: src/lib/api/with-api-envelope.ts:27 — withApiEnvelope always returns the { data, error, meta } envelope
src/lib/api/with-api-envelope.ts:40-45 — a PG SQLSTATE becomes DATABASE_ERROR; the raw message is never exposed

limitations.what: The admin_audit_log row this surface writes cannot be named in emits.ledger_events[].
limitations.measured: surface.schema.json's emits.ledger_events[] is closed to usage_events events; admin_audit_log is the second append-only ledger with no token, so emits.answer is "ledger" and the audit row is carried in breadcrumbs[] plus a ledger_row_present check (the admin_placements precedent).

limitations.what: Saved offers are not served into reports yet.
limitations.measured: No non-test source outside src/lib/placements and src/app/api/admin/placements reads offers (tripwire src/tests/placements-serving-tripwire.logic.test.ts); serving offers into the report response is the follow-up row (MF-40 D-7), which flips the tripwire deliberately.

notes: MF-40 (plan delta 1 section 5, folds 9 and 13). over_cap: an active offer whose group (the placement, plus the scenario pair for scenario_card) holds more active offers than max_slots (plan fold 8). resolvable: false for a scenario_card pair that is not a report scenario. Boolean and enum cells show content text <label>.option.<value>.

programme.why: The scheduled first-party offers of the admin placements page (MF-40).
